stages.sub: Why access to finance and owners' own goals shape whether a firm grows or stays small.

steps.q: A bank loan, selling shares, and keeping past profit are all ways a firm gets money from outside its own day-to-day trading. What would you call this whole group of options?
steps.right: Sources of money from outside the firm's normal trading
steps.wrong: Ways of cutting the firm's daily running costs
steps.hint: None of the three come from simply selling more product this week.

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: A small, unknown firm with few assets applies for a large loan and tries to attract new shareholders. Will banks and investors treat it the same as a large, established firm?
steps.right: No, it will find it much harder to get funded
steps.wrong: Yes, size makes no difference to lenders or investors
steps.hint: Think about how much a bank trusts a firm with no track record and few assets to offer as security.

steps.q: Because it struggles to raise loans or attract shareholders, and has little size to negotiate better deals with suppliers, what does a small firm end up facing compared with a large one?
steps.right: Weaker access to funding and weaker bargaining power
steps.wrong: Stronger access to funding and stronger bargaining power
steps.hint: Small firms buy less, so suppliers have less reason to offer them good terms, and lenders see them as riskier.

steps.q: A sole owner sells shares to outside investors to fund expansion. Those investors now want a say in decisions, and might want different things from the owner. If the owner instead stays small and keeps all the shares, what does she avoid?
steps.right: Investors pulling the business in a different direction from her
steps.wrong: Having to keep any accounting records at all
steps.hint: Think about what changes once someone else owns part of the decision-making power.

steps.q: An owner who values a relaxed lifestyle and enjoys running things her own way is offered a chance to expand fast, take on debt, and share control with new investors. Will her personal goals push her to take that chance, or to turn it down?
steps.right: Turn it down, to keep her lifestyle and control
steps.wrong: Take it, since growth is always the main goal
steps.hint: Growth would mean more pressure, more debt, and less control over decisions. Does that fit what she wants?
